summary: Focused revision of the applied batch-start refactor. idma_batch_start now: (1) rechecks deadline and signal inside the protected section after configuration but before the first NEXT_ID read, releasing both untriggered batch_started claims and launch stamps on expiry; (2) performs only the ordered A-then-V trigger reads and their ktime stamps with IRQs/preemption disabled; (3) restores first and then does commit bookkeeping outside the protected interval, with A0 releasing untriggered V before quarantining A, and V0 publishing the valid A commit before quarantining V so caller STOP/drain of A stays safe; (4) keeps the version=1 log contract and all trigger timestamps/raw IDs unchanged. idma_submit() again zeroes transfer_id on a failed NEXT_ID read so a failed ordinary submit never carries a stale ID. Harness work: the batch-start harness fixes the index-0 sentinel, asserts IRQ+preempt disabled at triggers and unprotected at config writes, injects the pending IRQ during the A trigger read and proves it stays unserviced until local_irq_restore (including a caller-entered-IRQ-disabled case where quarantine logging must not run inside the driver window), and adds post-config deadline/signal cases. Actual production drain verification on V-zero-after-valid-A is hosted in the scheduler harness (which already has production idma_drain plus the fake STOP/DONE/status batch model): one case proves A is stopped+drained+freed, one proves A is retained/quarantined when its drain times out, both prove V stays retained/unknown; the existing batch_zero_id case gains A-drain/free assertions.

/*
 * Bounded software batch start.  Both register sets are configured before any
 * NEXT_ID trigger.  Only the ordered A-then-V trigger reads, the software
 * timestamp reads and the per-stream commit bookkeeping run with IRQs and
 * preemption disabled.  The section is non-sleeping and never covers polling,
 * drain, quarantine, allocation, logging or cond_resched.
 *
 * a_triggered/v_triggered mean the corresponding NEXT_ID read was executed,
 * even when it returned zero.  a_id/v_id carry the raw readback (zero on
 * failure).  irq_span_ns is the ktime bracket around the protected trigger
 * reads; the real IRQ-off interval extends a bounded few instructions on both
 * sides and is not a cycle-accurate or interrupt-latency measurement.
 */
edits.new:
/*
 * Bounded software batch start.  Both register sets are configured before any
 * NEXT_ID trigger.  Only the ordered A-then-V trigger reads and their software
 * timestamps run with IRQs and preemption disabled.  That section is
 * non-sleeping and never covers commit bookkeeping, polling, drain,
 * quarantine, allocation, logging or cond_resched.
 *
 * The deadline and the pending signal are checked twice: once before the
 * configuration writes and again inside the protected section before the first
 * trigger.  A request that expires in between is dropped without triggering
 * either device, without keeping either untriggered batch_started claim and
 * without keeping their launch stamps.
 *
 * a_triggered/v_triggered mean the corresponding NEXT_ID read was executed,
 * even when it returned zero.  a_id/v_id carry the raw readback (zero on
 * failure).  irq_span_ns is the ktime bracket around the protected trigger
 * reads; the real IRQ-off interval extends a bounded few instructions on both
 * sides and is not a cycle-accurate or interrupt-latency measurement.
 *
 * Failure ownership matches the ordinary batch path: a stream whose trigger
 * read produced a valid ID is committed even when the other stream failed, so
 * the caller can still stop and drain it; a stream whose trigger read returned
 * zero is quarantined, and an untriggered V is released instead.
 */

risks: The mid-config deadline/signal cases depend on the harness time model: ktime_get_ns() advances 1000 ns per call and stall_after_conf_write forces now += 2 ms on the V CONF write; if that model changes, deadline_after_config/signal_after_config need re-derivation of their deadlines.
irq_service_ns == last_restore_ns assumes exactly one local_irq_save/local_irq_restore pair per idma_batch_start call, which holds today but would need updating if another save/restore is added.

A transfer's commit now runs after the protected section, so its deadline_ns is derived from the in-region a_end_ns timestamp rather than the post-restore moment; the logical transfer timeout is therefore computed a few instructions in the past. Contract preserved, but a reviewer should confirm this is acceptable for the 2 s xfer timeout.

The two new scheduler cases call idma_batch_start + idma_batch_stop + idma_drain directly and assemble the caller sequence in the harness; the production out_drain path itself is covered separately by the strengthened batch_zero_id assertions. Neither case calls idma_run_session end-to-end for the V-zero scenario.

batch_zero_id's new 'allocations - frees == 2' assertion assumes V retains exactly its two DMA allocations (src+dst) while A is freed; it would need revisiting if stream_prepare allocation accounting changes.

Batch-trigger path still does not zero transfer_id on a zero read (only the ordinary idma_submit path was specified); the failed batch stream is never in_flight, so the caller's drain is safe, but this asymmetry should be confirmed as intended by Codex.

The new post-config recheck runs ktime_get_ns() and signal_pending() with IRQs/preemption disabled; both are non-sleeping in Linux, but this is a Codex-level call on whether the signal check belongs inside the protected section on the target tree.
